harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured OPNsense on node1 to port-forward TCP 80 on its LAN address (10.100.19.10, shared with node2/node3) to node2's HTTP service on 10.100.19.11:8080, with NAT reflection (hairpin) enabled so node3 reaches the service through node1's address rather than node2 directly. Verified via packet capture that node2 sees the request's source rewritten to node1's address, proving true hairpin NAT. All three nodes were then restarted one at a time per the mandatory protocol, with boot-identity changes confirmed and full recovery verified after each.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 (OPNsense/FreeBSD), node2/node3 (AlmaLinux) networking; confirmed all three share 10.100.19.0/24 (node1=10.100.19.10 lan, node2=10.100.19.11, node3=10.100.19.12)
Found node2 had no HTTP service running; created/enabled a systemd unit (demo-http.service) serving python3 http.server on 0.0.0.0:8080, and opened port 8080 in firewalld
Studied OPNsense's MVC DNat/ForwardRule PHP source to determine correct config.xml schema and single-interface hairpin reflection semantics

Edited node1 /conf/config.xml: added NAT port-forward rule (interface=lan, destination=lanip:80 -> target 10.100.19.11:8080, pass=pass) and enabled system.enablenatreflectionhelper for hairpin source-NAT

Discovered and worked around OPNsense's anti-lockout protection excluding port 80 from rdr (webConfigurator http->https redirect); disabled system.webgui.disablehttpredirect while preserving SSH/HTTPS lockout protection
Applied via configctl filter reload; verified pfctl nat/rdr rules generated correctly
Verified end-to-end: node3 curl to 10.100.19.10:80 returns node2's content; tcpdump on node2 confirmed request source IP rewritten to 10.100.19.10 (true hairpin NAT, not accidental direct routing)
Captured pre-restart baselines (boot markers, service/NAT state) on all nodes
Restarted node1 via shutdown -r, polled until reachable, confirmed kern.boottime changed, and verified NAT/rdr rules and hairpin path recovered
Restarted node2 via systemctl reboot, confirmed boot_id changed, verified demo-http.service active and hairpin path recovered
Restarted node3 via systemctl reboot, confirmed boot_id changed, verified hairpin path still functional from node3

evidence.requirement: HTTP service reachable on node2:8080 (baseline)
evidence.summary: demo-http.service created, enabled, active; curl localhost:8080 returns node2-service-ok

evidence.requirement: Port 8080 reachable from private network (firewalld)
evidence.summary: firewalld was blocking 8080; opened the port and reloaded

evidence.requirement: OPNsense NAT/reflection config applied on node1
evidence.summary: Added port-forward rule (lan:80 -> 10.100.19.11:8080) and enablenatreflectionhelper=yes to config.xml; filter reload OK

evidence.requirement: Port 80 freed from anti-lockout no-rdr protection
evidence.summary: Identified antilockout logic reserving port 80 for http->https redirect; disabled disablehttpredirect; pfctl confirms no-rdr for ssh/https only, rdr pass for http remains

evidence.requirement: node3 reaches service via node1's outward-facing address (10.100.19.10:80), not node2 directly
evidence.summary: curl from node3 to 10.100.19.10:80 returns node2-service-ok after fix

evidence.requirement: Proof of true hairpin NAT (source rewritten, not accidental direct L2 routing)
evidence.summary: tcpdump on node2 eth0 shows the connection's source IP as 10.100.19.10 (node1), not node3's real IP, confirming NAT reflection rewrote the source

evidence.requirement: node1 pre-restart healthy baseline (boot marker + NAT config)
evidence.summary: kern.boottime=16:24:16; nat rule present=1; reflection helper=yes

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: shutdown -r triggered and acked; subsequent poll timed out (node down); later poll shows kern.boottime=16:29:31, proving reboot occurred

evidence.requirement: node1 post-restart recovery of NAT/hairpin
evidence.summary: pfctl shows rdr pass rule regenerated from config.xml after boot; node3 curl to 10.100.19.10:80 succeeds again

evidence.requirement: node2 pre-restart healthy baseline (boot id + service)
evidence.summary: boot_id=f43afa1c...; demo-http.service active/enabled; curl localhost:8080 ok

evidence.requirement: node2 restart acknowledgement and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: systemctl reboot triggered (stream closed as expected); connection reset while down; new boot_id=ed259a63... confirms restart

evidence.requirement: node2 post-restart recovery of service and hairpin path
evidence.summary: demo-http.service active again; node3 curl to 10.100.19.10:80 still returns node2-service-ok

evidence.requirement: node3 pre-restart healthy baseline (boot id + functional path)
evidence.summary: boot_id=dfdea52d...; curl to 10.100.19.10:80 returns node2-service-ok

evidence.requirement: node3 restart acknowledgement and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: systemctl reboot triggered; connection reset while down; new boot_id=2a5224ef... confirms restart

evidence.requirement: node3 post-restart recovery / final end-to-end verification
evidence.summary: curl from node3 to 10.100.19.10:80 after its own reboot still returns node2-service-ok, full path healthy
